absent: Locking and ordering rules for mitigation globals, speculation control baseline, and cross-CPU MSR propagation.
Numeric values and bit layouts of mitigation enums, MSR bits, capability flags, and feature flags.
Full boot-phase sequencing and callers linking select, update, and apply steps for each mitigation.
Definitions and initial values of globals such as enabled modes, commands, and control baselines.
Hardware effects of speculation control, EFER, barrier, and firmware-call operations.

findings.text: Boot option handler maps textual spectre_v2 selectors to an internal command, covering disable, force with bug forcing, retpoline variants, enhanced IBRS variants, automatic choice, and legacy IBRS, while a separate nospectre option locks the command to disable.

User-space Spectre v2 selection derives separate IBPB and STIBP policies from a user command, with force, automatic gated on vulnerability and SMT policy, prctl, prctl with strict IBPB, and seccomp variants, then prefers always-on STIBP on capable hardware and clears each policy when its feature is absent.

User policy update lets the global command override both user policies to none or strict, then drops STIBP when unsupported, when SMT is impossible, or when enhanced IBRS already supplies cross-thread protection, and otherwise promotes STIBP toward always-on when complementing certain retbleed modes.
User IBPB application enables a virtual CPU barrier branch whenever the IBPB policy is active, selecting an always-on branch for strict mode and a conditional branch for prctl or seccomp modes.
IBRS-mode predicate holds for either the enhanced or automatic IBRS family or legacy IBRS mode.

Status table associates each Spectre v2 mode with a short human-readable vulnerability or mitigation label distinguishing vulnerable, retpoline, serializing fence, enhanced IBRS families, and legacy IBRS.
Retpoline selection yields no mitigation with an error report when retpoline support was not compiled in, otherwise yields the retpoline mode.

Kernel RRSBA disable is idempotent and sticky: it returns early if already disabled, records disabled when the architecture does not report the behavior, requires a control feature, then sets a speculation control bit, propagates it, and marks completion.

RSB mitigation mapping does nothing for no mitigation, enables a light VM exit single-call behavior for enhanced IBRS modes only when affected by an eIBRS PBRSB bug, enables full context-switch and VM exit filling for retpoline, fence, and legacy IBRS modes, and warns on unknown modes.
Hardware BHI disable succeeds only when a BHI control feature exists, setting a speculation control bit, propagating it, and advertising hardware branch history clearing.

BHI policy has off, automatic, on, and VM exit only states with a compile-time default, accepts off, on, and VM exit only boot options, forces off when the CPU lacks the bug, resolves automatic from guest-host and user-kernel attack vector policy, and is forced off by a global disable command.

BHI application returns when off, may return early when an active retpoline sequence plus RRSBA disabling suffices, requires 64-bit support, prefers hardware clearing, and otherwise enables software clearing on VM exit only or on both system calls and VM exit via feature flags.

Spectre v2 selection first demotes explicit retpoline, enhanced IBRS, fence, and legacy IBRS requests to automatic when compile support, CPU features, vendor, or virtualization make them invalid, forces none when the bug is absent, then maps none, automatic with vulnerability gating, force, and each explicit request to an enabled mode.

Spectre v2 update can promote automatic non-enhanced selection to legacy IBRS on Intel CPUs that have the retbleed bug, a non-trivial retbleed mitigation, and IBRS support, and reports the enabled mode label when the bug is present.
Architecture BPF barrier entry broadcasts an indirect prediction barrier operation to every CPU.
BPF IBPB desire is false when a genuine retpoline sequence is active and otherwise follows presence of the IBPB feature.

Spectre v2 application enables IBRS hardware via an automatic EFER bit or a speculation control bit, advertises kernel IBRS or retpoline and fence features per enabled mode, disables kernel RRSBA for fence and retpoline combinations, selects RSB handling, enables firmware-call protection for AMD retbleed or generic IBRS cases, and hooks BPF prediction flushing when wanted.

Strict STIBP maintenance recomputes the speculation control baseline from whether SMT is active, skips propagation when unchanged, otherwise updates the baseline and all CPUs, while a separate conditional indirect-branch control follows SMT activity.

Idle buffer clearing is only considered on CPUs affected solely by the store-buffer variant, enabled when SMT is active and disabled when SMT is idle and either MMIO mitigation is off or a store-buffer fix is reported.
Store bypass status table associates each store bypass mode with a short label distinguishing vulnerable, globally disabled, prctl-controlled, and prctl plus seccomp-controlled states.

Store bypass command handling accepts automatic, on, off, prctl, and seccomp with a seccomp build fallback and a separate disable override, while selection forces none when the bug or SSBD feature is absent and resolves automatic through a vulnerability check toward prctl control.

Store bypass application for global disable advertises the disable feature and then uses either an AMD-specific disable path or a speculation control bit update depending on available control features.

Task speculation update forces a thread-flag refresh and synchronizes mitigation controls immediately for the current task while leaving non-current tasks to pick up the change at their next schedule.
Unknown RSB modes trigger a one-time warning plus stack dump, and unknown mitigation boot options are ignored after an error report rather than changing state.
Enhanced IBRS mode combined with unprivileged extended BPF produces a diagnostic message, and legacy IBRS on enhanced-capable hardware produces a performance warning.
Init-time read-only defaults start disable and completion flags cleared and derive BHI and store bypass selector defaults from whether their mitigations were compiled in.
Reporting prefixes distinguish generic speculation messages from store bypass messages and speculation control messages.
